profile.headline: Security and Collaborative Communications
profile.summary:
I currently work on security-related products for a small software company.

Previously, I worked in research and development of protocols and system architectures in the area of multimedia communications (voice, video, holographic videoconferencing, and data conferencing over IP) and security (encryption, hashing, identity management, and single sign-on).

In addition to architecture and software development activities, I did work in a number of standards and industry organizations, including the ITU, TIA, IETF, ETSI, and the IMTC. I served as a vice-chair for ITU-T SG16, chair of WP1/16 (multimedia systems), and rapporteur for the group that developed H.323. I have either authored or co-authored several standards in these various groups, including served as editor of the H.323 standard for multimedia communication over packet-based networks.

I co-founded Packetizer, which serves as a hub for information related to various technologies with a particular focus on collaboration and security.

Prior to getting into the telecom business, I wrote software for the healthcare industry, and developed and published my own software.

Specialties: Real-time multimedia communications (Voice Over IP, videoconferencing, telepresence, data collaboration) and security.

Patents: Total of 17.

positions.title: Software Engineer and Architect
positions.description: I focus on building software with an emphasis on security and collaboration. My work includes research and development in security-related technologies, as well as collaborating on software and hardware projects with external partners. At the outset, my role was to help shift the company’s focus from pure consulting toward a more product-oriented direction.

positions.title: Technical Leader, Security & Collaboration
positions.description:
Worked on a wide range of technologies as a member of the CTO Office for Collaboration and Security, including security-related protocols, Cisco Webex (especially cloud-based media servers and APIs), Webex Hologram, IOS-based routers, network protocols, quality of service, cloud services, and system architecture.

I actively engaged in the standardization of communication protocols for voice, video, security, fax, text, etc., working with the ITU-T, ETSI, ATIS, TIA, Cable Labs and other standards bodies. I served as editor for several technical protocol specifications, including H.323 and various IETF RFCs. I also chaired several standards committees during my time at Cisco, including Vice Chair of ITU-T SG16.

I designed some of the largest voice and video networks in the world, moving from there to video collaboration, holographic videoconferencing, and writing software and designing protocols to secure communications.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: DataBeam (acquired by IBM) was a great environment to work.  It was a young company with energetic, bright people trying to revolutionize the way people communicate and, they did.  It was at DataBeam where I got engaged in work on H.323 and SIP protocols, as well as web-based data collaboration systems.  Little did we know at the time that the technology we were building would turn into a multi-billion-dollar industry.

positions.title: Programmer
positions.description: As the largest hospital in the Easter Seal family, I continued my work on healthcare-related software systems, with the work expanded to include a very wide range of software, inclduding billing, functional evaluation, medical records, addmission coordination, and payroll.  I also worked on software to integrate with other systems (e.g., pharmacy system), wrote software to allow employees to work off-line (remotely) and synchronize with the central systems, etc. And since Cardinal Hill is relatively small (and very short on programming staff), I also had the opportunity to set up and manage most of the Internet services used by the hospital, including connections USENET and email services.  (Boy, how far things have come since then...)

positions.title: Programmer
positions.description: I was a software developer on a medical software system, responsible for re-writing significant parts of the system and developing new functionality in preparation for a major new system release.
